served.bankWhy: Paragraph 3 lists his two findings, and the second is that in every sample the amount of adenine closely matched the amount of thymine, and guanine matched cytosine.

proof.quote: the amount of adenine closely matched the amount of thymine

distractorNotes: Too strong: only the paired bases matched each other; nothing says all four were present in equal amounts.
Reversed: paragraph 3 says the proportions differed from one species to another.
Outside the passage: no fixed fraction for adenine plus thymine is mentioned.
Outside the passage: paper chromatography separated the bases, and nothing is said about removing the sugar first.

answer.text: the amount of adenine in a sample closely matched the amount of thymine
answer.line: Paragraph 3 gives two findings. The second: in every sample, adenine closely matched thymine and guanine matched cytosine.

steps: Find Chargaff in paragraph 3. He has two findings, marked First and Second. Hold both.
The second finding is the answer: inside each sample, adenine matched thymine.
Use the first finding as a filter. The proportions differed from species to species, so any choice that makes every species alike is out.

choices.text: the amount of adenine in a sample closely matched the amount of thymine
choices.note: Paragraph 3, sentence 4, nearly word for word.

choices.text: the four bases were present in equal amounts in the DNA of every species
choices.note: The match is in pairs: adenine with thymine, guanine with cytosine. All four equal goes further, and sentence 3 says the mix differed between species.

choices.text: the DNA of all species contained the same proportions of the four bases
choices.note: Paragraph 3 says the opposite: the proportions differed from one species to another. That first finding is what brought down the fixed-repeat idea.

choices.text: adenine and thymine together made up a fixed fraction of every sample
choices.note: Adenine and thymine are paired, but no fixed share holds in every sample: the mix changed from species to species.

choices.text: the bases could be separated only after the sugar had been removed
choices.note: Nothing in paragraph 3 says the sugar had to come off first. Paper chromatography simply separated the bases.
